guardrail: A runtime guardrail flags the call — a threshold breach or an anomaly at the tool-call boundary — that can trip the breaker.
telemetry: Observability turns the agent's behaviour into a signal, so a defined anomaly or threshold breach, or a manual pull, trips the breaker.
breaker: A circuit breaker at the tool-call boundary trips on a defined signal — a threshold breach, an anomaly, or a manual pull — and is tested on a schedule.
agentA: The misbehaving or compromised agent whose scope is revoked, halting just its tool calls because it is bound to its own identity.
agentB: Another agent in the fleet, unaffected by the revocation, which keeps running.
agentC: A further agent in the fleet, also unaffected, so containment stops one agent without breaking the rest.
record: The trip is logged as a machine-readable incident record, so containing the agent is itself an evidence event.
